about: S5 2s.2: the corpus paths that are configured in the expanded composition but executed by no scenario in it, pinned on the owner's answer (ii) of 2026-09-14 so that a NEW gap fails tests/corpus-configured-paths.test.js loudly. What a path is, and what executing means, are stated in that test. The list only shrinks. It is corpus record content, like tools/control-corpus.json: a corpus change that makes a gap execute removes the gap here, in that corpus commit. Adding a name needs the test's frozen copy of the list edited too, which is an instrument change.
pinnedAtMeans: The commit whose corpus was measured when the list was pinned. A file cannot name the commit that contains it.

why.retirement.guytonSkipInflation: Set in 40 scenarios and executed in none. The corpus holds one guyton plan, and no negative prior-year return reaches its decision.
why.retirement.preserveRoth: Set in 5 scenarios and executed in none since S5AA R50. seed:19 was the one that executed it: its owner's Roth IRA holds no entered basis, and with preserveRoth off the optimizer drew the Roth at 45, which turning it on moved later. Since R50 (AA1-36, the Roth IRA basis ledger) such a draw is taxed earnings with the 10%, and the optimizer's ledger weight already ranks the Roth behind the HSA for that owner, so the switch no longer changes seed:19's draws. The path itself still executes on a plan built to reach it (the test's reaching plan, at 66).

shrunk.in: S5 2s.1's corpus commit (Q73 / U4, under Q77 (a))
shrunk.why: The repaired stage draw revives the plans that never reached these branches: seed:1 is no longer $0 from its first row, so its preTax -> taxable transfer runs, and a revived plan takes rule 55. tests/corpus-configured-paths.test.js measures both executing in the repaired corpus.

The carried spending base is now the unadjusted amount, so a stage adjusts the year it applies to instead of compounding into every later year. Staged fixedReal plans no longer collapse toward zero spending, so they reach the withdrawal-ordering branch this path controls. The same cause removed advanced.rule55 and the preTax -> taxable transfer in S5 2s.1's corpus commit: a spending defect was suppressing corpus coverage of real code, and repairing it restores the coverage rather than reducing it. tests/corpus-configured-paths.test.js measures it executing in the repaired corpus.

regrown.why: Not a corpus change: an engine rule (the R50 Roth ledger's optimizer weight) made the switch's only corpus counterfactual coincide with the plan. It was removed in S5AA task 2.1's corpus commit and is re-pinned here, within the test's frozen copy (GAPS_WHEN_PINNED), so the shrink-only test still holds; a corpus scenario that reaches the switch again removes it.
